'''''Maclura tricuspidata''''' is a [[tree]] native to central and southern China, Korea, and Vietnam.<ref name = powo/> It is occasionally grown for its [[fruit]], somewhat similar to that of the related [[mulberry]] (''Morus'' spp.).

== Common names ==

Among its common names are Chinese mulberry (but not to be confused with ''[[Morus australis]]'' also known by that name), storehousebush, mandarin melon berry, silkworm thorn, ''cudrang'', ''kkujibbong'' (Korean 꾸지뽕), ''zhe'' or ''che'' ({{zh|c={{linktext|柘}}|p=zhè}}).{{citation needed|date=June 2024}}

== Description ==
It grows up to 6 m high.

The [[Tanzhe Temple]] west of [[Beijing]], [[China]] is named for this tree.

==Uses==
Aside from its edible fruit,<ref>{{Cite web |title=Growing Mandarin Melon Berry / Che: Maclura tricuspidata |url=https://gardenoracle.com/images/maclura-tricuspidata.html |access-date=2023-06-02 |website=gardenoracle.com}}</ref> which can also be used to make wine, the tree has several other uses. In China, its leaves are fed to [[silkworm]]s, its bark is used to make [[paper]] and a reddish-yellow [[dye]], and its roots are used for medicinal purposes. Its wood is also valuable, and is used for the construction of [[Bow and arrow|bows]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Cudrania tricuspidata Silkworm Thorn, Storehousebush PFAF Plant Database |url=https://pfaf.org/user/Plant.aspx?LatinName=Cudrania+tricuspidata |access-date=2023-06-02 |website=pfaf.org}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Maclura tricuspidata in Flora of China @ efloras.org |url=http://www.efloras.org/florataxon.aspx?flora_id=2&taxon_id=242331085 |access-date=2023-06-02 |website=www.efloras.org}}</ref>

==Fossil record==
[[Fossil]]s similar to ''Maclura tricuspidata'' have been collected from the [[Eocene]] of [[France]], [[Miocene]] of [[Bulgaria]], [[Pliocene]] of [[China]], and [[Quaternary]] of [[Japan]].<ref>{{cite journal|journal=Review of Palaeobotany and Palynology|volume=140|pages=113–122|year=2006|title=Maclura (Moraceae) wood from the Miocene of the Baja California Peninsula, Mexico: Fossil and biogeographic history of its closer allies|vauthors=Martinez Cabrera HI, Cevallos-Ferriz SR |issue=1–2|url=https://www.researchgate.net/publication/292995365|doi=10.1016/j.revpalbo.2006.03.004}}</ref>
